title: AVD Infrastructure 1
description: Friday night Sev1. Overnight users cannot launch desktops from one host pool. The client shows they cannot connect.
scope: Out-of-hours Sev1: users cannot connect to a production AVD host pool.
illustrativeDisclaimer: This scenario, its mock incident, runbook titles, escalation routes, and organisational procedures are illustrative. Validate them against approved operational sources before use. They are not bank-specific policy.
assessorGuidance: Reward a calm first response: confirm blast radius, consult the connectivity runbook, check Azure Service Health and session host status, and engage Microsoft when control-plane evidence appears — without requiring the engineer to personally restore Microsoft services. Accept more than one valid investigation order if reasoning and evidence are sound. Safety-critical: do not restart all session hosts or make platform-wide changes without a plan and appropriate authority.
acceptableAlternativeApproaches: Starting with Service Health and the connectivity runbook, then confirming host pool blast radius.
Starting with a live user symptom and affected CI, then checking Service Health before changing hosts.
Opening a Microsoft case in parallel with MIM notification when control-plane degradation is already visible.

questions.prompt: Walk through how you would handle this incident from the first call through to recovery. Write the full response in your own words.
questions.helpText: Users cannot connect to one pool. Think about what you would check first, and what you would not change on the estate.
questions.assessorGuidance: Score the whole write-up. Reward confirming blast radius and protecting existing sessions before host changes; using the connectivity runbook and Azure Service Health; treating AVD control plane / gateway in UK South as the leading domain while still checking this pool’s agent health; engaging MIM and Microsoft with case facts (pool, region, error codes, impact) rather than trying to restore a Microsoft fault personally; a factual stakeholder update; and recovery confirmed with a new user connection plus host status, not Service Health wording alone. Do not score as demonstrated: reboot or rebuild every host as a first action; a company-wide DNS story as the primary cause; waiting to fix it personally before raising Microsoft/MIM.

scoringCriteria.label: Establishes blast radius and customer impact before making platform changes
Uses Sev1 OOH process, including MIM and a managed investigation
Engages Microsoft with appropriate evidence when control-plane symptoms appear
Interprets host pool, gateway, and connection evidence in a sound order
Keeps networking in view without forcing an unsupported company-wide DNS story
Uses the connectivity runbook and known diagnostic sources rather than improvising
Uses the support model instead of attempting to personally restore a Microsoft fault
Produces a factual update and confirms recovery with users
Avoids unsafe mass host restarts or rebuilds during an undiagnosed Sev1
